ns2:course.label: Latin America Cultural Studies II
ns2:course.description: Panoramic view of Latin American cultures since the end of the colonial period (roughly 1820) to the present. Examination of the major debates, authors and cultural issues that shaped those cultures or that were shaped by them. Specific themes may vary by semester, and may include the following: slavery, colonialism and neocolonialism, revolution, mestizaje, gender, the state, and modernization. Analysis will include diverse cultural phenomena, as well as consideration of cultural perspectives and practices. Instruction in Spanish unless otherwise noted. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 6 hours, if topics vary. Prerequisite: SPAN 228 or consent of instructor.
